title: Three rules for the opening
line: Take the center, bring out the knights and bishops, castle.

steps.text: Three rules for the first moves: put pawns in the center, bring out the knights and bishops, and castle.
Take the center: push one of the middle pawns two squares.

wrong.h2h4: A pawn on the edge does nothing for the center.

steps.hint: The middle pawns stand in front of your queen and king.
steps.after: A pawn in the center takes squares away from the other side's pieces.

steps.text: Bring out a knight toward the center.

wrong.g1h3: From the edge the knight reaches fewer squares and does not touch the center.
wrong.b1a3: From the edge the knight reaches fewer squares and does not touch the center.

steps.after: From there a knight covers two center squares.

steps.text: Now a bishop, to a square where it aims at Black's side and clears the way to castle.
steps.after: The bishop is out, and nothing stands between the king and the rook on h1.

steps.text: Castle. The king is safe on g1, and the rook comes toward the middle.
steps.after: A center pawn, two pieces out, the king castled. Black is following the same rules.

steps.text: Here Black broke a rule: the pawn move to f6 guards e5, but it takes the knight's best square and opens the way to the king.
White takes on e5 with the knight. If the pawn takes it, as most club players do, that is a second slip: now the black king stands open.
Check with the queen on h5.
steps.hint: The queen reaches the ringed square along a diagonal.
steps.after: The pawn on g6 blocks, and the pawn on e5 has lost its guard.

steps.text: Take on e5 with check. The rook on h8 is next.
steps.after: The queen attacks the king and the rook at once. Black is losing the rook.

summary: Pawns to the center, knights and bishops out, king castled. Moves that skip these hand the other side time.
